newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks rise 1.29 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks rise 1.29 pct in late trade.

text.p: Active buying in Taiwan's star electronics sector and China-concept stocks pushed share prices sharply higher in late Friday trade, brokers said.
With 60 minutes left, at 0300 GMT, the index was up 106.10 points or 1.29 percent at 8,337.40. Turnover was T$86 billion.
Electronics surged 2.79 percent, partly reflecting U.S. high-tech shares' overnight rebound, with chipmaker United Microelectronics up T$2 to T$84, brokers said.
China-concept shares -- Taiwan firms with active or planned investments in the communist Chinese mainland -- were strong, and those in electronics even more so.
China-linked power supply maker Liton Electronic surged the daily seven percent limit to T$101.5

"As electronics and China-concept shares emerged as trendsetting shares to lead the overall upward momentum, the index likely is ready to launch another round of rally," said HSBC James Capel analyst Alex Chen.
"Many institutional investors have turned their recent short positions to active buying, and that really boosts overall sentiment," Chen said.
